stories.title: McLaren boss praises Norris-Piastri 'harmony' as the champions chase a struggling 2026 car
stories.what_happened: McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said in a team Q&A this week that he is proud of how Norris and Piastri have handled the aftermath of their intense 2025 title fight, saying the harmony between the two drivers — and with the wider team — has actually strengthened rather than frayed. This comes as McLaren has struggled to find pace under 2026's new technical regulations, trailing Mercedes and Ferrari so far this season despite entering as reigning champions. Piastri said he remains confident the team can engineer the kind of mid-season improvement it has pulled off in previous seasons.
key_points: McLaren team principal **Andrea Stella** says the relationship between title rivals **Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri** has only grown stronger since their 2025 title fight.
Norris won the **2025 championship**, overturning a **34-point deficit** to Piastri with nine races left — one of the closest finishes in years.
McLaren has been **off the pace in 2026** under all-new technical regulations, with **Mercedes and Ferrari** currently ahead.
Piastri says he's **'confident'** McLaren can repeat the kind of mid-season turnaround it has managed in past years.

depth.background: McLaren enters 2026 as the defending constructors' and drivers' champions after Lando Norris beat teammate Oscar Piastri and Red Bull's Max Verstappen in a tense three-way title battle last season — notable because Piastri had led by 34 points with nine races to go before losing out. Formula 1 introduced a major regulation overhaul for 2026 covering both chassis and engine rules, which has reshuffled the competitive order; early reports suggest Mercedes and Ferrari have adapted better than McLaren so far this season.

stories.title: Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is now active — he can leave for 2027 if he chooses
stories.what_happened: Multiple outlets reported this week that Verstappen's exit clause has now been triggered, since he heads into the 2026 summer break in sixth place in the drivers' championship — about 110 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli — outside whatever top-two or top-three threshold the clause requires (reports vary on the exact cutoff). This makes him free, in principle, to test the open market and negotiate a move for 2027, though he has said publicly he wants to fulfil his Red Bull contract through 2028 if the team can show real progress. Red Bull remains winless in 2026, its first season with its own in-house engine after years of Honda power.
key_points: Verstappen's Red Bull contract includes a **performance clause** tied to his championship position at the **summer break**.
He is currently **sixth in the standings**, about **110 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli** — well outside the clause's threshold.
That means the clause has now **triggered**, making him a **free agent** who can negotiate a 2027 move without Red Bull's consent.
Red Bull remains **winless in 2026** with its first in-house engine, adding pressure on the team to convince him to stay.

depth.background: Max Verstappen, a four-time F1 world champion, lost the 2025 title to McLaren's Lando Norris after years of Red Bull dominance, and 2026 brought a major regulation reset that has left Red Bull struggling — this is also the team's first season running its own in-house power unit rather than a Honda-supplied engine. Verstappen's contract runs through 2028, but it reportedly contains a performance-linked exit clause letting him leave early if the team falls outside a specified championship position by the summer break. Rival teams, especially Mercedes and Aston Martin, have been circling amid persistent rumors about his future.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported a NASCAR team owner had confirmed talks about Verstappen's F1 future were real, with a decision expected to land around his home Dutch Grand Prix later this month.
thread.changed: Today it's confirmed that the underlying trigger — Verstappen's championship position at the summer break — has actually been met, meaning the exit clause is now formally active rather than just a subject of rumor.

stories.title: F1 boss Domenicali says a German Grand Prix return is now 'definitely' happening — but not before 2029
stories.what_happened: F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali said Formula 1 has renewed contact with Hockenheim representatives about a potential calendar return, calling Germany a 'very interesting market' for the sport's future. He stressed any return would be **'mid-term, not short-term'** — F1's calendar is already set through 2028, meaning the earliest realistic date is **2029**. The renewed interest follows a change in ownership at Hockenheim: the **Emodrom Group** acquired a **74.99% stake** in the circuit's operating company in 2024, a shift Domenicali suggested has made the venue a more credible commercial partner.
key_points: F1 CEO **Stefano Domenicali** confirmed talks are underway to bring the **German Grand Prix back to the calendar**, most likely at the historic **Hockenheim** circuit.
Domenicali called it a matter of **'when, rather than if'**, saying 'it will not be a short-term call, but definitely will happen.'
F1's calendar is **locked in through 2028**, so a German GP return couldn't realistically happen before **2029**.
Talks follow a change of ownership at Hockenheim, where the **Emodrom Group bought a 74.99% stake** in the circuit's operator in 2024.
Germany hasn't hosted a round since **2019**, despite producing champions like **Michael Schumacher and Sebastian Vettel**.

depth.background: The German Grand Prix is one of F1's most historic races, having crowned champions at circuits like Hockenheim and the Nürburgring for decades, and it was the home race for two of the sport's most successful drivers, Michael Schumacher and Sebastian Vettel. It dropped off the calendar after 2019 amid low attendance, high hosting fees, and competition from newer, better-funded races in the Middle East and Asia. F1 has since expanded to a record number of races, with persistent fan and sponsor pressure to bring a German round back given the size of the German car industry and fanbase.

stories.title: Charles Leclerc admits he once thought Max Verstappen was a 'bad person' — and is open to partnering him at Ferrari
stories.what_happened: In a wide-ranging interview, Charles Leclerc said that as a teenager racing against Verstappen in karting, he genuinely believed **Verstappen was 'a bad person'** — a view Verstappen reportedly held of Leclerc too at the time. Leclerc said growing older taught both drivers that people can be very different away from the heat of competition, and that their relationship has since transformed even though their on-track battles remain fierce. Asked directly about the swirling speculation that Verstappen could join him at **Ferrari**, Leclerc said he would welcome, not resist, the partnership — notable given team-mate rivalries are often a source of tension in F1. The comments land amid a summer of intense **Verstappen-to-Ferrari transfer talk**, with his Red Bull future reportedly set to be decided around his home Dutch Grand Prix in late August.
key_points: **Charles Leclerc** revealed he used to believe rival **Max Verstappen** was 'a bad person', dating back to when they raced each other as karting teenagers.
Leclerc says the two have since realised **people are different off the track** than they seem while racing wheel-to-wheel.
Leclerc confirmed he **would not shy away** from partnering Verstappen at **Ferrari** if the Dutchman's rumoured move materialises.
Speculation over **Verstappen's future** has intensified amid reports his Red Bull deal could be revisited around his **home Dutch Grand Prix** later this month.
On-track, Leclerc says their rivalry **'stays on the circuit'** even as their personal relationship has warmed.

depth.background: Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc are two of Formula 1's biggest stars and fierce on-track rivals, with a history of contentious wheel-to-wheel battles going back to their karting days. Verstappen, a four-time world champion with Red Bull, has been the subject of persistent driver-market speculation this season amid reports of internal Red Bull tension and interest from rival teams, including Ferrari, where Leclerc has been the lead driver since 2019. Any Verstappen-to-Ferrari move would be one of the biggest driver transfers in the sport's history.

stories.title: Danube drought forces Hungary and Romania's first-ever nuclear reactor shutdowns as WWII wrecks resurface
stories.what_happened: Water levels on the **Danube** kept falling through the first week of August, with flow near Romania measured at roughly **2,900 cubic meters per second — far below the seasonal average of 4,600**. For the first time in either country's history, **Hungary and Romania** were forced to shut down or scale back nuclear reactors that rely on Danube water for cooling. Romanian navy engineers detonated **180 kilograms (397 lbs) of submerged rock** in the riverbed to redirect what water remains toward the intake for the country's nuclear reactor. As the water retreated, around **20 WWII-era German shipwrecks** — broken masts and corroded hulls scuttled near Prahovo, Serbia, in 1944 — rose back into view, drawing tourists out in small boats. The same drought exposed a woolly mammoth's bones in Bulgaria last week. Governments across the region are now urging households and industry to conserve electricity as multiple national power grids edge toward emergency status.
key_points: Danube's low flow forced **nuclear reactor** shutdowns in two countries.
Hungary and Romania cut reactor output for the **first time ever**.
Romania detonated **180 kilograms** of rock to redirect cooling water.
Dozens of **WWII-era German warships**, scuttled in 1944, have resurfaced.
River flow near Romania is about **2,900 m³/s**, well below average.

depth.background: The **Danube River** is Europe's second-longest river, flowing through ten countries and supplying drinking water, irrigation, shipping routes, and cooling water for nuclear power plants across Central and Eastern Europe. A summer of extreme heatwaves and almost no rain has pushed the river to some of its **lowest levels on record**, a crisis that has been building since late July. Near **Prahovo, Serbia**, Germany's Black Sea fleet deliberately scuttled roughly 200 ships in September 1944 to slow the Soviet advance — wrecks that only resurface when the river runs unusually low. The drought had already pushed Hungary's only nuclear plant toward emergency measures before this week's escalation.

thread.previously: Hungary's only nuclear plant was nearing a forced shutdown as the Danube fell to record lows during Europe's heatwave.
thread.changed: Hungary and Romania have now actually shut down or scaled back Danube-cooled reactors for the first time on record, Romania blew up riverbed rock to save its plant's cooling intake, and the falling river has exposed WWII-era shipwrecks and a mammoth's remains as the crisis spreads.

stories.title: Delhi's swine flu cases jump six-fold this monsoon, with dengue climbing alongside it
stories.what_happened: Delhi's health department has recorded **1,349 H1N1 cases** so far this season, up sharply from just **229 cases** at the same point last year — roughly a **six-fold increase**. Alongside it, the city has logged **1,379 dengue cases**, of which about **200 patients** traveled in from outside Delhi for treatment. Delhi's health minister, Pankaj Singh, said **no fatalities** have been recorded from either disease so far this year, and that government hospitals are fully prepared to handle the rising patient load. Health officials have linked the twin rise to the ongoing **monsoon season** and its effect on both mosquito breeding and viral spread.
key_points: Delhi has logged **1,349 H1N1 (swine flu) cases** this season, versus **229** by the same point last year — nearly a **six-fold jump**.
The city has also recorded **1,379 dengue cases**, including roughly **200 patients from outside Delhi**.
Delhi's health minister said **no deaths** have been recorded from either illness this year.
Government hospitals say they are **'fully prepared'** to handle the rising caseload.
Both illnesses are **monsoon-linked**, spreading faster with stagnant water and humid conditions.

depth.background: Delhi sees a **seasonal spike** in both **H1N1 influenza (swine flu)** and **dengue fever** every monsoon, as heavy rain leaves pools of stagnant water where dengue-carrying mosquitoes breed, while humid, crowded conditions help respiratory viruses like H1N1 spread more easily. Case counts vary sharply year to year, which makes this year's jump from last year's comparatively low numbers look especially steep.

stories.title: India captain Shubman Gill ruled out of Sri Lanka warm-up as squad injury crisis deepens
stories.what_happened: India captain **Shubman Gill** did not take the field on **Day 1** of India's three-day warm-up fixture against a Sri Lanka Cricket XI in Colombo, after sustaining a **right ring finger injury** during practice. With Gill unavailable, vice-captain **KL Rahul** led the side, after Sri Lanka Cricket XI won the toss and chose to bat first. The absence compounds an already-stretched bowling attack: strike bowler **Jasprit Bumrah** is missing the tour entirely with a knee injury. In response, India have handed uncapped seamer **Auqib Nabi** a maiden **Test squad call-up**. The three-day warm-up match is India's only real preparation before the two-Test series opens in Galle on **August 15**.
key_points: **Shubman Gill** injured his **right ring finger** in practice and sat out **Day 1** of India's three-day warm-up match against Sri Lanka Cricket XI.
Vice-captain **KL Rahul** led the side instead, after **SLC XI won the toss** and chose to bat first.
India are already missing pace spearhead **Jasprit Bumrah**, who is out with a **knee injury**.
Uncapped seamer **Auqib Nabi** has been given a maiden **Test call-up** to cover the gap.
The warm-up is India's key preparation for the **two-Test series starting August 15 in Galle**, on spin-friendly Sri Lankan pitches.

depth.background: India's tour of Sri Lanka centers on a two-Test series beginning **August 15 in Galle**, where India historically has to adjust quickly to **spin-friendly, low, turning pitches** very different from home conditions. Ahead of the series, captain Shubman Gill had already taken **two blows to the hand** during nets in Colombo, though scans at the time cleared him to continue. This latest issue — a separate finger injury sustained during the warm-up match itself — adds to a growing list of fitness concerns just as the tour gets underway.

stories.title: SK Hynix commits $38 billion to two new memory-chip plants as AI demand outruns supply
stories.what_happened: SK Hynix's board approved 54 trillion won ($38 billion) in new investment to build two fabrication plants: Yongin Y2, a DRAM facility getting 35.2 trillion won and focused on high-bandwidth memory and advanced DRAM, and Cheongju M17, a NAND flash plant getting 19.1 trillion won. Construction on the DRAM plant is set to begin in July 2027 with its first cleanroom online by June 2029; the NAND plant breaks ground in February 2027 with its first cleanroom targeted for December 2028. The company said it has accelerated its target to complete all four Yongin fabs by 2033, twelve years earlier than the original 2045 plan. The move responds to what the company and analysts describe as an AI-driven memory shortage that shows no sign of easing.
key_points: SK Hynix's board approved **54 trillion won ($38 billion)** to build two new fabrication plants — one for DRAM, one for NAND flash.
The bigger plant, **Yongin Y2**, gets **35.2 trillion won** and will focus on high-bandwidth memory, the specialized chips AI data centers need most.
The second plant, **Cheongju M17**, gets **19.1 trillion won** for NAND flash production.
SK Hynix has pulled forward its full Yongin buildout timeline **from 2045 to 2033** — a **12-year acceleration** — chasing AI-driven demand.

depth.background: SK Hynix is one of the world's three dominant memory-chip makers, alongside Samsung and Micron, and has become a key supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) — specialized, ultra-fast memory stacked next to AI processors like Nvidia's GPUs. As AI data-center buildouts have accelerated worldwide, demand for this memory has outpaced supply, pushing up prices and lead times industry-wide. This investment is the newest installment of a 'master plan' SK Hynix announced last year to invest 600 trillion won in its Yongin Semiconductor Cluster and 100 trillion won expanding its Cheongju base.

stories.title: Centre reportedly plans a special Parliament session to push the Delimitation Bill again — government denies it
stories.what_happened: Multiple outlets reported this week, citing sources, that the Centre is planning to call a three-day special Parliament session from August 16 to 18 specifically to push through the Delimitation Bill and the Women's Reservation Amendment Bill, with the government working to secure the two-thirds majority it lacked in April. Prime Minister Modi reportedly told NDA MPs the alliance now has the numbers to proceed. However, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju publicly denied the reports, telling ANI there is 'no proposal to extend any dates of Parliament Session, no Special Session from August 16 to 18' on either bill. The Delimitation Bill would raise the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats, with 815 elected from states and 35 from union territories.
key_points: Sources say the Centre is planning a **3-day special Parliament session from August 16-18** to take up the Delimitation and Women's Reservation Bills.
The Delimitation Bill would expand the **Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 seats** — a nearly **60% increase** in national lawmakers.
This would be the **second attempt**: the same Constitution Amendment Bill was **voted down in April 2026** for lack of numbers.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister **Kiren Rijiju has denied** any special session is planned, contradicting the sourced reports.

depth.background: India's Lok Sabha (lower house of Parliament) seat count has been frozen at 543 since the 1970s even as the population has grown substantially, creating long-standing pressure to 'delimit' — redraw and expand — constituencies to reflect current population. The government introduced the Delimitation Bill and the linked Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in April 2026, but the constitutional amendment failed to get the required two-thirds majority on April 17 and was withdrawn. Opposition parties, especially from southern states, have resisted expansion plans that could shift parliamentary power toward more populous northern states.

stories.title: RBI proposes ban on revolving credit for NBFCs, Bajaj Finance shares crash 5.5%
stories.what_happened: On Thursday, the RBI released draft amendments to its NBFC credit rules proposing that non-bank lenders offer only **term loans** — a fixed amount repaid on a set schedule, not reusable once repaid — and stop offering revolving credit products altogether, except for the two NBFCs licensed to issue credit cards (SBI Card and BoB Cards). Investors reacted fast: Bajaj Finance shares tumbled as much as **5.5%** on the BSE on Friday, wiping out over **₹33,500 crore** in market value in roughly an hour. Analysts at IIFL estimate revolving-style flexi-loans make up **around 15%** of Bajaj Finance's loan book, making it more exposed than rivals. Other NBFCs — Tata Capital, L&T Finance, Poonawalla Fincorp — also fell, dragging the Nifty Financial Services index down over 1%. The RBI is taking public comments until August 28, so the rule isn't final yet.
key_points: RBI draft bars NBFCs from offering **revolving credit**, only term loans allowed
Bajaj Finance shares crashed **5.5%**, erasing over ₹33,500 crore in market value
Exemption: only **SBI Card** and BoB Cards can still offer revolving credit
Flexi-loans make up roughly **15%** of Bajaj Finance's loan book, per IIFL
Public comments open until **August 28** before the rule is finalized

depth.background: India's shadow banks — non-banking financial companies or **NBFCs** — form a massive parallel lending system, financing everything from gadgets to small-business working capital, often under lighter rules than banks. Since the 2018 collapse of infrastructure lender **IL&FS** exposed shadow-banking risks, the RBI has steadily tightened NBFC rules to close gaps with bank supervision. A **revolving credit** facility — like a credit card — lets a borrower repay and re-borrow the same limit repeatedly, which regulators worry can mask risk. Bajaj Finance, India's largest NBFC by market value, built much of its growth on 'flexi-loan' products that work exactly this way.

stories.title: India and China hold border talks to prevent 'miscalculation' along the LAC
stories.what_happened: India and China held the **36th meeting of the WMCC** in New Delhi on Thursday, with the Indian side led by Joint Secretary (East Asia) **Sujit Ghosh** and the Chinese delegation led by **Hou Yanqi**, Director General of China's Boundary and Oceanic Affairs Department. India's Ministry of External Affairs said in a Friday statement that both sides reviewed the overall situation along the LAC to maintain 'peace and tranquillity' in border areas. India reiterated its request for an early meeting of the Expert Level Mechanism on trans-border rivers and pressed China to share **technical details of its upstream infrastructure projects**. The two sides also discussed broader boundary and border-management issues.
key_points: India and China held their **36th WMCC meeting** in Delhi on Thursday to discuss the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**.
India pressed China again for **technical details on its upstream dam projects** on rivers flowing into India.
Both sides agreed peace along the border underpins **wider bilateral ties**, the MEA said.
The talks are part of a **slow normalization** since the deadly 2020 Galwan clash froze relations.

depth.background: India and China have disputed their roughly 3,500-km Himalayan border for decades, and relations froze after a deadly clash between troops in the **Galwan Valley in 2020**. The **Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC)** is a standing diplomatic channel, below the level of military commanders, that both sides use to manage day-to-day friction along the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)** — the de facto, undemarcated border. China's plans to build a mega hydropower dam on the Yarlung Tsangpo river (which becomes the Brahmaputra in India) have been a growing concern for New Delhi, since upstream control gives China leverage over water flow into India's northeast.

stories.title: Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan sign a NATO-style mutual defence pact in Mecca
stories.what_happened: On **Friday in Mecca**, Turkish President **Recep Tayyip Erdogan**, Saudi Crown Prince and PM **Mohammed bin Salman**, and Pakistani PM **Shehbaz Sharif** signed the **Mecca Joint Deterrence Agreement**. The pact states that 'any armed attack' on one signatory will be treated as an attack on all three — the same mutual-defence logic behind **NATO's Article 5**. A Turkish official described it as 'purely defensive in nature', and reports suggest it could open the door to joint military exercises, technology transfers and intelligence-sharing among the three militaries. Officials say the deal is unlikely to formally extend Pakistan's nuclear umbrella to Saudi Arabia and Turkey, since Islamabad's nuclear posture remains focused on India — but any adversary weighing an attack on Riyadh or Ankara must now reckon with a **nuclear-armed Pakistan** having pledged to treat that as an attack on itself. India's foreign ministry said New Delhi is watching the agreement's implications closely, given it hands its nuclear rival new collective-defence commitments.
key_points: The **Mecca Joint Deterrence Agreement**, signed by Erdogan, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and PM Shehbaz Sharif, declares an attack on any one signatory an **attack on all three**.

It links the world's only **nuclear-armed Muslim state (Pakistan)**, the top oil exporter **Saudi Arabia**, and NATO's **second-largest military, Turkey**, under one security umbrella for the first time.
The pact builds on a **2025 Saudi-Pakistan mutual defence deal**, now widened to include Turkey.
**India's foreign ministry** said it is 'closely following' the implications of its rival Pakistan gaining new collective-defence partners.
Analysts read the timing as a **signal to Israel**, long suspected to be the region's only nuclear power, amid the ongoing Iran-Israel-US standoff.

depth.background: Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a bilateral mutual-defence pact in September 2025, extending a decades-old security relationship — Pakistani troops have trained and been stationed in Saudi Arabia for years, and Riyadh has long bankrolled Islamabad. **Turkey**, a NATO member with the alliance's second-largest army, has separately been courting closer defence ties with Riyadh amid its own tensions with Israel over Gaza and Syria. The **Iran-Israel-US conflict** simmering through 2026, including strikes and disputes over the Strait of Hormuz, has pushed Gulf and Muslim-majority states to hedge with new deterrence arrangements rather than rely solely on the US security umbrella.

stories.title: Afghanistan thrash Ireland by 126 runs to level their ODI series after Tuesday's total washout
stories.what_happened: Afghanistan beat Ireland by **126 runs** in the second ODI at Bready Cricket Club on Friday, leveling the rain-disrupted series at **1-1**. **Hashmatullah Shahzad** scored a century and **Rahmat Shah**, leading Afghanistan's new-look ODI side, also played a substantial innings to set up a big total. In reply, Afghanistan captain **Gulbadin Naib** took **6 wickets for 43 runs** — the third-best bowling figures by any Afghan bowler in ODI history — to dismantle Ireland's chase. Ireland had recalled captain **Paul Stirling** after he recovered from injury, though seamer Joshua Little remained unavailable, but the hosts were never in the contest against Afghanistan's total.
key_points: Afghanistan beat Ireland by **126 runs** in the 2nd ODI at Bready, leveling the 5-match series at **1-1** (after the opener was abandoned without a ball bowled).
**Hashmatullah Shahzad** scored a century and **Rahmat Shah** — leading Afghanistan in a new captaincy era — also contributed a strong knock.
Captain **Gulbadin Naib** took **6 for 43**, the third-best bowling figures in Afghanistan's ODI history.
Ireland brought back captain **Paul Stirling** from injury for the match, but Afghanistan's total proved well out of reach.
Three matches remain in the series, all still to be played at the **same Bready venue**.

depth.background: Ireland and Afghanistan are playing a 5-match ODI series that both teams have framed as an important early test for their new captaincy setups — the series opener on August 5 was **abandoned without a ball bowled** after continuous rain prevented even a toss from taking place, leaving the series at 0-0 heading into the second game. **Rahmat Shah** is leading Afghanistan in a new leadership era for the format, while Ireland's regular captain **Paul Stirling** had been out through injury.

thread.previously: The series opener, scheduled for 10:45am local time at Bready, never got underway after continuous morning rain prevented even a toss — officials abandoned the match around midday, leaving the 5-match series locked at 0-0 with both teams set to try again on Friday.
thread.changed: Friday's rescheduled second match went ahead in full, and Afghanistan won by 126 runs behind a Hashmatullah Shahzad century and a near-record 6-for-43 from captain Gulbadin Naib, leveling the series at 1-1 with three matches left to decide it.

stories.title: IMD issues red alert for Odisha as a fresh Bay of Bengal low threatens extremely heavy rain
stories.what_happened: The India Meteorological Department issued a red warning for Odisha late on August 6, forecasting heavy to very heavy rain with isolated extremely heavy spells over the following 24 hours. The trigger is an upper-air cyclonic circulation currently sitting over south Gangetic West Bengal and adjoining Bangladesh, which is expected to spawn a new low-pressure area over the coastal Bay of Bengal. The IMD has advised residents and local authorities in the affected districts to stay alert given the risk of flooding and disruption to normal life as the active monsoon spell continues.
key_points: The IMD issued a **red alert** warning of **extremely heavy rainfall** in isolated parts of Odisha over the next 24 hours.
An **upper-air cyclonic circulation over Gangetic West Bengal and Bangladesh** is expected to trigger a fresh **low-pressure area** in the north-west Bay of Bengal.
The warning is **valid until 8:30 am on August 8**, covering several coastal and interior districts.
Odisha's monsoon has already been **active for days**, raising the risk of waterlogging, flash floods, and landslides in low-lying areas.

depth.background: India's east coast, including Odisha, sits directly in the path of Bay of Bengal weather systems that intensify through the monsoon season (June–September). Low-pressure areas forming in the bay routinely bring the region's heaviest rain spells, and Odisha has a history of severe monsoon flooding in its river deltas. The IMD grades rainfall warnings by colour, with **red being the most severe**, signalling authorities should take immediate action.

stories.title: Sikandar Raza's blazing cameo powers MI London past London Spirit in fiery Hundred derby
stories.what_happened: On August 6 at Lord's, MI London beat London Spirit by four wickets in a feisty London derby in the Men's Hundred. Chasing Spirit's 160 for 5 (built around a Wiaan/Pretorius knock of 52, David Willey's 31 and James Coles' unbeaten 30), MI London got home at **164 for 6** with six balls to spare. Raza produced the decisive burst, hitting his first, fourth and seventh balls for six — one of them a **105-metre** strike off Coles that almost cleared Lord's — to finish with 32 off just 16 balls and take Player of the Match. Nicholas Pooran (39) and Sam Curran (33) supported the chase. The win pushed MI London up to **second** in the men's table, while it officially knocked Spirit out of playoff contention — the first team, men's or women's, eliminated this season. Players from both sides were seen exchanging words as they left the field.
key_points: Raza smashed **32 off 16 balls**, sixes off his 1st, 4th, 7th balls
MI London chased down **161**, winning by **4 wickets** at Lord's
One Raza six flew a colossal **105 metres**, nearly clearing the ground
Loss makes Spirit the **first team** (men's or women's) out of the playoffs
Players **exchanged words** leaving the field after a heated contest

depth.background: **The Hundred** is England's 100-ball franchise tournament, now in its late-season run where every result decides who reaches the knockouts. **London Spirit** and **MI London** are the competition's two London-based rivals, so any game between them carries extra needle on top of the table stakes. Zimbabwe's **Sikandar Raza** is a franchise-circuit specialist known for turning games in a handful of overs.

stories.title: Amelia Kerr's 69 off 41 balls rescues MI London from 64 for 8 to snap a long winless run
stories.what_happened: **MI London Women** beat **London Spirit** by **3 runs** in a dramatic London derby at Lord's on Thursday, picking up their **first win of the season**. MI London's innings nearly fell apart, collapsing to **64 for 8** with wickets tumbling around them, before **Amelia Kerr** held one end together and produced a match-turning innings of **69 off 41 balls**. The result moves MI London level with Spirit on **six points** and keeps their qualification hopes alive, while Spirit's home form continues to slide — they have now lost **six matches in a row** at their home ground across two seasons.
key_points: **MI London Women** beat London Spirit by **3 runs** at Lord's in The Hundred.
MI London collapsed to **64 for 8** before **Amelia Kerr's** innings turned the match around.
Kerr scored **69 off 41 balls**, the standout performance of the game.
The win is MI London's **first of the season**, keeping their campaign alive.
London Spirit have now lost **six matches in a row** at home across two seasons.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-format cricket competition, played in 100-ball innings, with both men's and women's tournaments running simultaneously each August. MI London Women, owned by the Mumbai Indians group, had struggled to find form so far this season, while local rivals London Spirit were chasing a home win to end a lengthy losing streak of their own — making Thursday's London derby at Lord's unusually high-stakes for both sides' campaigns.

stories.title: New Zealand star Sophie Devine ruled out for the rest of The Hundred with a calf injury
stories.what_happened: Sophie Devine sustained a calf injury while playing for **Welsh Fire** in their defeat to Birmingham Phoenix, and has now been ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 Hundred season. Welsh Fire have signed New Zealand teammate **Orla Prendergast** as her replacement for the rest of the campaign. The news comes alongside another significant injury blow in the competition, with England's **Danni Wyatt-Hodge** also ruled out of MI London's Hundred campaign.
key_points: Devine injured her **calf** playing for Welsh Fire against Birmingham Phoenix.
She's now ruled out for the **rest of the 2026 Hundred season**.
**Orla Prendergast** has been named as her replacement.
It follows another injury blow: **Danni Wyatt-Hodge** also ruled out of MI London's campaign.
The 2026 Hundred season runs **July 21 to August 16**.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-format 100-ball cricket competition, running men's and women's tournaments each summer with franchise teams across UK cities. New Zealand international **Sophie Devine**, a veteran all-rounder, has been a regular overseas signing in the women's competition. Injuries to overseas and star players are common across the tightly-packed global T20 calendar, where players shuttle between leagues with little recovery time.

stories.title: North Korea fires first ballistic missile in weeks, days before US-South Korea drills
stories.what_happened: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said North Korea fired a **short-range ballistic missile** from the eastern coastal area of **Wonsan** at around 5 p.m. local time on Thursday, August 6. The missile flew out over the water and landed in the sea off North Korea's east coast; officials said it did not cross into Japanese territorial waters or airspace and posed no immediate threat to South Korea, Japan or US forces in the region. It was the **first ballistic missile test since late June**, when North Korea tested a tactical missile with a special warhead. South Korea's military raised its surveillance posture and said it is coordinating closely with the United States and Japan to analyze the launch. The test came just **days before** the annual US-South Korea Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises are set to begin later in August. North Korea has previously called these drills a rehearsal for invasion and often responds to them with weapons tests.
key_points: North Korea launched a **short-range ballistic missile** Thursday evening.
It flew from **Wonsan**, landing in the sea off North Korea's coast.
No missile reached **Japanese** territorial waters or airspace, officials said.
This is North Korea's first launch since **late June**.
It comes days before annual **US-South Korea** military drills begin.

depth.background: North Korea has spent decades developing short- and medium-range missiles that can reach South Korea and Japan, and it typically tests them to protest joint US-South Korea military drills, which Pyongyang calls rehearsals for invasion. **Kim Jong Un's** regime had gone quiet on missile launches for about **six weeks**, since a **late-June** test of a tactical ballistic missile carrying a 'special mission' warhead. Every August, the US and South Korea hold large-scale exercises — this year's **Ulchi Freedom Shield** drills are due to begin later in the month — and North Korea has a long history of firing missiles just before or during them. Seoul, Washington and Tokyo track every launch closely because it also reveals how North Korea's missile technology is progressing.

stories.title: LIC's profit jumps 23% to ₹13,492 crore as its most profitable growth metric surges 61%
stories.what_happened: LIC's board approved its Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026) results on August 6, in a meeting held from 2:45 PM to 4:55 PM IST. The insurer reported a standalone net profit of ₹13,492 crore, up 22.81% from ₹10,986 crore in the same quarter last year. Total premium income rose 6.75% to ₹1,27,250 crore. The more closely watched metric, Value of New Business (VNB) — an estimate of the future profit locked in from policies sold this quarter — jumped 61.32% to ₹3,136 crore, while the VNB margin expanded 750 basis points to 22.9% from 15.4% a year earlier, a sharp improvement in how profitable LIC's new business mix is. LIC retained its dominant 60.10% market share of first-year premium income, and its solvency ratio — a measure of its ability to pay out future claims — improved to 242% from 217% a year earlier. The company hosted an investor earnings call at 7:00 PM IST the same evening to discuss the results.
key_points: LIC's **net profit rose 22.81%** year-on-year to **₹13,492 crore** for the June quarter (Q1 FY27).
**Value of New Business (VNB)** — a measure of future profit from new policies — jumped **61.32%** to ₹3,136 crore.
Its **VNB margin expanded by 750 basis points**, from 15.4% to **22.9%**, meaning each new policy is now far more profitable.
LIC still commands a **60.10% market share** of first-year premium income, keeping it India's dominant life insurer.
Its **solvency ratio improved to 242%**, well above the regulatory minimum, from 217% a year earlier.

depth.background: LIC (Life Insurance Corporation of India) is India's state-owned life insurance giant and the country's largest institutional investor, so its quarterly results are watched both as a corporate earnings report and as a read on Indian household savings behaviour. Since its 2022 stock market listing, investors have focused less on LIC's sheer size and more on whether it can improve its **VNB margin** — historically lower than private rivals like HDFC Life and SBI Life — because that margin shows how profitable each new policy actually is, not just how many are sold.

stories.title: Shubman Gill takes two blows to the hand in Colombo nets, but scans clear him ahead of the Sri Lanka Tests
stories.what_happened: During a training session in Colombo on **Thursday**, Gill copped two separate blows in the space of an afternoon. The first came in the nets, where a throwdown from uncapped young pacer **Gurnoor Brar** struck him on the right thumb; Gill went off to have it strapped by the team physiotherapist before returning to complete his batting work against spinners. The second blow came later during a slip-catching drill, when he misjudged a sharp catch and took an impact to the hand, forcing him to stop and apply an ice pack. Team management had preliminary scans and assessments done, which showed **no fracture or structural damage** — a relief for a squad already thin on senior personnel. Gill was able to finish the day's training without significant discomfort, and reports indicate he remains on track to lead the side into the series opener.
key_points: Gill was hit on the **right thumb** by pacer Gurnoor Brar during a nets session in Colombo on Thursday.
He left briefly to get it **strapped by the team physio**, then came back to face spinners.
A second blow followed later — this time to the hand during a **slip-catching drill** — forcing an ice pack.
Preliminary checks found **no fracture or structural damage**; he completed training without major discomfort.
The scare lands right as India is already missing **Jasprit Bumrah** (knee injury) for the series.

depth.background: Shubman Gill is on his first tour as India's full-time Test captain, and this Sri Lanka series is his first assignment in the role. India already arrived short-handed: strike bowler **Jasprit Bumrah** was ruled out with a knee injury picked up fielding in England, and the squad is missing several other regulars too. The tour opened with a three-day warm-up match against a Sri Lanka XI at Colombo's NCC ground (August 7-9), a tune-up before the first of two Tests begins in **Galle on August 15**.

thread.previously: India's Test squad, already missing pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah to a knee injury and several other regulars, opened its Sri Lanka tour with a three-day warm-up match in Colombo — the first assignment of Shubman Gill's tenure as full-time Test captain.
thread.changed: During Thursday's training in Colombo, Gill took two separate blows to his right hand — one in the nets, one in a slip-catching drill — but preliminary scans found no fracture, and he's on track to be fit for the series.

stories.title: Uganda's parliament approves troops for the Gaza peacekeeping force, with Morocco also pledging soldiers
stories.what_happened: Uganda's parliament voted Thursday to approve deploying its armed forces (the UPDF) to Gaza as part of the ISF, becoming one of the first countries to formally commit. Morocco has also pledged troops separately, making these the first African nations to sign on to the mission. The force overall is designed to reach **20,000 troops** and will be commanded by American **Major General Jasper Jeffers**. Its mandate covers three things: providing basic security in Gaza, training and standing up a new Palestinian police force, and overseeing the demilitarization and reconstruction of the territory. The force was originally proposed by President Trump's Board of Peace back in February 2026, as part of the broader Gaza peace plan Israel and Hamas signed in October 2025.
key_points: Uganda's parliament approved sending **UPDF troops** to Gaza as part of an international stabilization mission.
Morocco has separately **pledged troops** too — the first African contributors to the force.
The planned force is meant to be **20,000-strong**, led by American Major General Jasper Jeffers.
It comes from the **Gaza peace plan** Israel and Hamas agreed to in **October 2025**.
Its job: provide security, **train a new Palestinian police force**, and oversee demilitarization.

depth.background: After two years of war, Israel and Hamas agreed to a ceasefire and peace framework in October 2025, brokered heavily by the Trump administration. Part of that deal was creating an **International Stabilization Force (ISF)** — a UN-mandated multinational peacekeeping force — to secure Gaza once fighting stopped, since neither Israel nor Hamas can be trusted to police the territory themselves. The idea was first proposed by Trump's **'Board of Peace'** in February 2026. Getting countries to actually commit troops has been the hard part — nobody wants to be blamed if it goes wrong.

stories.title: Government reveals Modi's foreign trips have cost ₹74.58 crore so far in 2026, over ₹550 crore since 2021
stories.what_happened: Minister of State for External Affairs Pabitra Margherita told the Rajya Sabha on Thursday that expenditure on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's foreign visits has reached over **₹74.58 crore** in 2026 so far, while cumulative spending on his overseas trips since 2021 stands at more than **₹550 crore**. The costliest leg disclosed for this year was the Norway stop of a five-nation tour in May, at ₹17.46 crore. The year-wise breakdown showed spending of over ₹180 crore in 2025, ₹109 crore in 2024, ₹93 crore in 2023, ₹55 crore in 2022, and ₹36 crore in 2021 — a broadly rising trend. The MEA also said 316 memoranda of understanding and agreements have been signed during the PM's foreign visits since July 2021.
key_points: The government told the **Rajya Sabha** that PM Modi's foreign visits have cost **₹74.58 crore** so far in 2026.
Cumulative spending on his overseas trips since 2021 has crossed **₹550 crore** across 77 countries.
The costliest single stop this year was the **Norway leg** of a five-nation tour in May, at ₹17.46 crore.
Annual costs have climbed steadily, from ₹36 crore in 2021 to over **₹180 crore in 2025**.
The government also disclosed **316 memoranda of understanding** were signed on these trips since July 2021.

depth.background: In India's parliamentary system, the government must answer written questions from MPs in the **Rajya Sabha** (Parliament's upper house) and Lok Sabha (the lower house), and these answers are a common way spending details — like the cost of a prime minister's travel — become public. Opposition MPs frequently use these questions to scrutinize executive expenses, especially around high-profile foreign trips, since the money spent is public money. This particular answer came from the **Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)**, in response to a question during the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament.

stories.title: Lok Sabha passes Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill 2026 without debate amid opposition protests
stories.what_happened: The Lok Sabha passed the **'Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026'** on Thursday, August 6, moved by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. The bill was approved by **voice vote without any discussion**, as opposition members continued protests demanding action over police handling of a July 20 demonstration, rather than debating the bill's contents. The legislation amends the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007**, the **Income-tax Act 2025**, and the **Finance Act 2026**, and will formally replace the **Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026** that the government had issued earlier this year. Among its provisions: extending tax incentives for electronics manufacturing, exempting foreign institutional investors from tax on income from government securities, and measures to support the diamond trade.
key_points: The bill amends the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007**, the **Income-tax Act 2025**, and the **Finance Act 2026**.
It passed by **voice vote with no discussion**, as opposition MPs protested over unrelated issues.
It will **replace the Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026**, an emergency measure the government had issued earlier.
Key proposals **extend electronics-manufacturing tax incentives**, **exempt foreign investors from tax on government securities**, and support the **diamond trade**.

depth.background: India's government had earlier issued the **Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026** — a temporary law the President can issue when Parliament isn't in session, which must later be replaced by an actual Act passed by Parliament or it lapses. This bill is that replacement, folding the ordinance's provisions into permanent law alongside other tax tweaks. Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** piloted the bill through the Lok Sabha (the lower house of India's Parliament) during the ongoing Monsoon Session, which has been repeatedly disrupted by opposition protests over unrelated issues, including police action against protestors on July 20.

stories.title: India's new stock-closing system passes its first big test, calming fears after last week's wild Nifty swings
stories.what_happened: Today was the Sensex's first weekly derivatives (F&O) expiry priced entirely under the new CAS. Under this system, buy and sell orders placed near the close are matched in a single-price auction, and that auction price becomes the official closing price — instead of an average of the last 30 minutes of regular trading. The session held steady: the Sensex closed at 78,954.75, up 0.48%, only marginally above where it stood just before the auction began. The Nifty 50 moved a mere 0.03% during the auction itself — a sharp contrast to the volatility seen on the system's chaotic debut day.
key_points: The **Sensex's first weekly expiry** under the new Closing Auction System (CAS) passed **largely without disruption** today.
The Sensex closed **0.48% higher** at 78,954.75, just **0.2% above** its pre-auction 3:15pm level.
The Nifty 50 moved just **0.03%** during the closing auction itself, easing fears of another chaotic swing.
**SEBI's CAS**, live since Monday, replaced the old method of averaging trades over the final 30 minutes.
Analysts say the earlier turbulence should be **temporary** as traders adjust to the new mechanism.

depth.background: **SEBI**, India's markets regulator, introduced the Closing Auction Session (CAS) this week to fix how closing/settlement prices are calculated on options-expiry days, after the system's debut caused wild, unexplained swings in the Nifty that traders blamed on the old method being exploitable near the close. SEBI initially said it found **'no design flaws'** in the new system but promised close monitoring as it rolled out further.

thread.previously: Yesterday, SEBI defended its new Closing Auction System after it caused wild, unexplained Nifty swings on its first options-expiry day, saying it found no design flaws.
thread.changed: Today's first full weekly Sensex expiry under the same system passed smoothly — Sensex and Nifty barely moved during the auction — easing fears the chaos would repeat.
