stories.title: Ireland and Afghanistan open a new era under new captains as a 5-match ODI series begins in Bready
stories.what_happened: The two sides begin a **5-match ODI series** on August 5, with the first two matches at **Bready Cricket Club** and the final three at the **Civil Service Cricket Club in Belfast**, running through August 15. Afghanistan will be led by their newly appointed ODI and Test captain **Rahmat Shah**, with explosive wicketkeeper-batter **Rahmanullah Gurbaz** as his deputy, while Ireland will be captained by veteran opener **Paul Stirling**. All five matches start at 10:45am local time. Afghanistan arrive as strong favorites, having won the last six ODIs between the two sides.
key_points: A **5-match ODI series** between Ireland and Afghanistan runs **August 5 to 15** across Bready and Belfast
Afghanistan are led by newly appointed captain **Rahmat Shah**, with **Rahmanullah Gurbaz** as vice-captain
Ireland are captained by **Paul Stirling**
**Afghanistan have won their last 6 ODIs** against Ireland heading into this series
First two matches at **Bready Cricket Club**, remaining three at **Belfast's Civil Service Cricket Club**

depth.background: Ireland and Afghanistan are both full ICC members who play each other periodically, with Afghanistan having built one of the world's stronger white-ball sides in recent years despite the country's limited domestic infrastructure. Both teams go into this series under **freshly appointed captains** — a notable change for each side as they look toward the next World Cup cycle. Afghanistan's recent ODI dominance over Ireland, with 6 straight wins, sets up this series as a real test of whether Ireland's new leadership can close that gap.

stories.title: ICC bans USA cricketer Akhilesh Reddy for 8 years after he deleted evidence in a T10 corruption probe
stories.what_happened: An ICC Anti-Corruption Tribunal found USA player Akhilesh Reddy guilty of multiple breaches connected to the **2025 Abu Dhabi T10 League** and banned him for **eight years**. The tribunal ruled he attempted to influence the conduct of matches and encouraged another player — referred to as "Player A" — to take part in corrupt activity. Investigators also found Reddy deliberately deleted WhatsApp messages and call records exchanged with that player before the ICC's investigation began, in an apparent attempt to destroy evidence. Reddy told the tribunal he routinely wiped data from his phone as standard "data hygiene," but the tribunal rejected that explanation and ruled the deletions were intentional obstruction. His suspension is backdated to **21 November 2025**.
key_points: The **ICC's Anti-Corruption Tribunal** banned USA player **Akhilesh Reddy, 26,** for **eight years** over corruption in the **2025 Abu Dhabi T10 League**.
He was found guilty of **trying to influence match conduct** and **encouraging another player** to engage in corrupt activity.
The tribunal found he **deliberately deleted WhatsApp messages and call logs** with a fellow player to obstruct the investigation.
Reddy claimed the deletions were routine **'data hygiene'** — the tribunal **rejected that explanation**.
The ban is **backdated to 21 November 2025**, when his suspension began.

depth.background: The Abu Dhabi T10 League, a short, franchise-based T10 tournament in the UAE, has repeatedly been a target of match-fixing investigations because of its fast format and heavy betting-market attention — the ICC has banned multiple players and officials connected to the tournament over the years. The ICC's Anti-Corruption Code prohibits fixing or attempting to fix match outcomes, and separately punishes obstructing an investigation, such as destroying evidence, just as harshly as the corrupt act itself. Reddy is a USA international cricketer, and his ban is a reminder that anti-corruption scrutiny extends well beyond the biggest leagues like the IPL.

stories.title: Senate committee advances Trump's attorney general pick Todd Blanche, 12-10, after he scraps a controversial $1.8 billion fund
stories.what_happened: The Senate Judiciary Committee voted **12-10 along party lines** on Tuesday to advance Blanche's nomination to the full Senate for a final confirmation vote. The breakthrough came after Republican Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis, who had threatened to block the nomination, agreed to support it once Blanche formally **rescinded the $1.8 billion fund in writing** over the weekend. Despite that concession, Republican Senator **Susan Collins** of Maine announced she will vote no on the floor, saying the Justice Department "has become increasingly political" and that Blanche's own actions had "further eroded the Department's independence." No Democrats on the committee supported the nomination. The vote clears the way for a floor vote later this week, though Collins' opposition shows Blanche still faces resistance within his own party.
key_points: The Senate Judiciary Committee voted **12-10 along party lines** to send Blanche's nomination to the full Senate
Two GOP holdouts backed him only after he agreed to **kill a $1.8 billion 'anti-weaponization' fund**
Republican Sen. **Susan Collins** says she will still vote no, citing DOJ independence
Blanche is currently **acting attorney general** and was previously Trump's personal defense lawyer

depth.background: Todd Blanche has been serving as acting U.S. Attorney General and was previously one of Donald Trump's personal criminal-defense lawyers before joining the administration. As acting AG, he set up a controversial **$1.8 billion fund**, informally called the "anti-weaponization fund," which critics said gave the Justice Department broad, discretionary power that could reward allies or punish opponents. His formal nomination to hold the job permanently has been stuck in the Senate Judiciary Committee over objections from within his own party about that fund and about DOJ independence more broadly.

stories.title: Supreme Court orders RBI to draft rules within 4 weeks to crack down on 'mule accounts' used in digital-arrest scams
stories.what_happened: A Supreme Court bench headed by **Chief Justice of India Surya Kant**, with Justices **Joymalya Bagchi** and **V Mohana**, ordered the RBI to prepare and circulate a **Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)** for handling mule accounts and accounts linked to money laundering and cyber fraud, within **four weeks**. The order requires the SOP to be sent to the **Registrar General of every High Court** in the country, aligning courts nationwide on how banks should detect, freeze and act on suspicious accounts. The directions are part of a broader set of nationwide measures the court has been issuing to fight the surge in digital-arrest scams, which have cost Indian victims — including elderly citizens — enormous sums.
key_points: The **Supreme Court** directed the **RBI** to prepare a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on mule accounts within **four weeks**.
The order came from a bench led by **Chief Justice Surya Kant**, as part of a nationwide crackdown on **"digital arrest" scams**.
A **mule account** is a bank account used to receive and launder scam money — often without the account holder's knowledge.
The case began after a **senior citizen couple** told the court they lost their life savings to a digital-arrest scam.
The RBI's final SOP must also be shared with the **Registrar General of every High Court** nationwide.

depth.background: "Digital arrest" scams are frauds where callers impersonate police or government officials, falsely tell victims they're under investigation, and pressure them into transferring money to "prove their innocence" — the money is then funneled through **mule accounts**, ordinary bank accounts (sometimes belonging to unwitting people, sometimes rented out for a fee) used to receive and quickly move stolen funds before they can be traced. The Supreme Court took up this issue **suo motu** (on its own initiative) after a senior citizen couple told the court they were defrauded of their life savings through exactly this kind of scam, and has since been issuing directions to tighten India's response.

stories.title: Delhi Police stop Kejriwal's march to PM Modi's residence over E20 ethanol-blended petrol
stories.what_happened: On the morning of **August 4**, Arvind Kejriwal led roughly **100 AAP workers and leaders**, including Manish Sisodia and Jasmine Shah, on a march toward Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence. Their goal was to formally submit over **2.3 lakh petitions** gathered from citizens across India opposing the government's E20 ethanol-blended petrol policy, which they say is hurting vehicle owners. **Delhi Police intercepted and stopped the march** on Firoz Shah Road before it could reach the PM's residence, having deployed a heavy security presence of Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel in anticipation. Blocked from proceeding, Kejriwal and the other leaders **sat down in protest on the road**. Kejriwal said afterward that he would **intensify** the campaign against the E20 mandate rather than stand down.
key_points: **Arvind Kejriwal** and about **100 AAP supporters** tried to march to **PM Modi's residence** to hand over petitions against **E20 petrol**.
They carried more than **2.3 lakh (230,000) petitions** collected from citizens nationwide opposing the ethanol-blended fuel policy.
**Delhi Police stopped the march** on Firoz Shah Road, deploying heavy security including paramilitary forces.
Former Delhi deputy CM **Manish Sisodia** and AAP's **Jasmine Shah** sat down in protest after being blocked.
Kejriwal vowed to **intensify the campaign** against the Centre's E20 policy rather than back down.

depth.background: **E20 petrol** is petrol blended with **20% ethanol**, part of the central government's push to cut oil imports and vehicle emissions by mixing biofuel into every litre sold at the pump. AAP, which lost power in Delhi but remains a vocal opposition force, has campaigned against the mandate, arguing ethanol-blended fuel **damages engines and reduces mileage** in older vehicles, a claim the government disputes. Kejriwal, AAP's national convenor, has increasingly used street marches and petition drives to keep pressure on the BJP-led central government since leaving Delhi's chief ministership.

stories.title: Pro-Kannada groups call a Karnataka-wide bandh for August 13 over a fresh order to release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu
stories.what_happened: Pro-Kannada organisations have called for a statewide bandh (shutdown) in Karnataka on **August 13**, running from **6am to 6pm**, to protest a CWMA directive ordering the state to release **3,500 cusecs of Cauvery water per day to Tamil Nadu for 15 days**. Activist Vatal Nagaraj said the shutdown has the backing of more than **1,600 Kannada organisations** and over **1,000 other groups** across the state, arguing that Karnataka itself is short on water and that the release will hurt local farmers who depend on the same river for irrigation. The Kannada film industry has also thrown its support behind the bandh call. The protest adds to a summer already marked by heavy flooding and monsoon disruption elsewhere in Karnataka and neighboring states.
key_points: Over **1,600 Kannada organisations** have called for a bandh across Karnataka on **August 13**, from 6am to 6pm.
The trigger: a **Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA)** order directing Karnataka to release **3,500 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days**.
Activists argue Karnataka itself is facing **water scarcity** and that the release would hurt local farmers.
The **Kannada film industry** has publicly extended support to the bandh call.
This is the latest flashpoint in a **decades-old inter-state dispute** over sharing the Cauvery river's water.

depth.background: The Cauvery river dispute is one of India's oldest and most politically charged inter-state water conflicts, pitting Karnataka (upstream) against Tamil Nadu (downstream) over how much river water each state can use, mainly for irrigation and drinking supply. The Supreme Court eventually settled the sharing formula and created the **Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA)** to enforce it, but on-the-ground compliance remains a recurring flashpoint whenever water levels run low, and past bandh calls over the issue have shut down Bengaluru and other Karnataka cities before.

stories.title: Kimi Antonelli opens up on how pressure 'destroyed' him during his brutal rookie F1 season
stories.what_happened: In an interview released **August 4** as part of SAP's 'Significant Figures' series, Antonelli spoke candidly about the toll of his rookie Formula 1 season, saying the sheer pace of new experiences felt like **'driving three seasons at once'** — overwhelming both physically and mentally. He said the pressure of the role at points **'kind of destroyed'** him, particularly during a difficult stretch in the European leg of the season when he felt he was letting down the people who had backed him, including Wolff, who fast-tracked him into the seat. Antonelli said he has since found ways to manage that pressure better and feels the experience has made him stronger going into the current season. Fellow young driver Arvid Lindblad separately praised Antonelli's 'pure racing instincts' in comments carried the same day.
key_points: Antonelli said the learning curve felt like **'driving three seasons at once'** — mentally and physically overwhelming.
He admitted the pressure of replacing **Lewis Hamilton** at Mercedes **'kind of destroyed'** him at points in his debut season.
The toughest stretch came during the **European leg** of the campaign, when he felt he was **letting down** those who believed in him.
He says the experience has made him **stronger** heading into this season.
The comments came in an **SAP-sponsored interview series** released **August 4**, during F1's summer break.

depth.background: Kimi Antonelli was thrust into one of the most scrutinized seats in Formula 1 when **Mercedes** picked him to replace seven-time champion **Lewis Hamilton**, who left for Ferrari — a decision Mercedes boss Toto Wolff made before Antonelli had even raced in Formula 2, the feeder series most drivers use to prove themselves first. That vote of confidence came with enormous pressure: comparisons to Hamilton, and to teammate **George Russell**, followed him into every race weekend of his rookie campaign.

stories.title: Sergio Perez says Cadillac's rookie-season struggles come down to a lack of in-house development, not just pace
stories.what_happened: Perez explained that Cadillac's persistent gap to the midfield — currently around **2.5 seconds a lap**, with the team about **one second off** the cars just ahead — is driven partly by **'inefficiency'** and partly by the fact that a lot of development work is **outsourced to third parties** rather than done in-house, limiting how fast the team can iterate. A **significant upgrade package introduced at the Austrian Grand Prix** was meant to close that gap but has left the team's competitive position largely unchanged. Team technical figure **Pat Symonds** separately conducted an extensive review of Bottas's car after Bottas underperformed Perez by more than expected, given both arrived with similar credentials, going through the car 'top to bottom' looking for a technical explanation. Both drivers say the team needs either a major development breakthrough or a stroke of luck to score Cadillac's first championship points.
key_points: **Cadillac**, F1's brand-new team this season, remains roughly **one second per lap** off the midfield despite continuous car updates.
**Sergio Perez** says the gap is partly down to **'inefficiency'** and a lack of development done in-house, since Cadillac outsources much of its car design to third parties.
A big upgrade package introduced in **Austria** hasn't closed the gap as much as hoped.
Team veteran **Pat Symonds** has been probing why teammate **Valtteri Bottas** has struggled even more than Perez despite similar experience.
Both drivers say Cadillac needs a **'big step' or some luck** to score its first championship points.

depth.background: **Cadillac** joined the F1 grid as a brand-new team in 2026, a rare and difficult undertaking since building a competitive car from scratch normally takes years even for well-funded operations. Unlike established teams, Cadillac doesn't yet have full in-house design and manufacturing capability for every component, so it relies on **third-party suppliers** for parts of its car — which slows how quickly it can react to weaknesses. **Sergio Perez**, a former Red Bull driver, and **Valtteri Bottas**, a former Mercedes driver, were signed specifically for their experience to help the new team find its feet.

stories.title: Litton Das recovers in time, added to Bangladesh's Test squad for the Australia series opener
stories.what_happened: The Bangladesh Cricket Board named wicketkeeper-batter **Litton Das** in the squad for the first Test against Australia, after he recovered from a calf injury faster than initially expected. Das was originally left out of the tour's opening fixtures following the injury, sustained during the June ODI series against Australia, but has now been cleared to join the squad in Darwin ahead of the series opener. The squad, captained by **Najmul Hossain Shanto** with **Mehidy Hasan Miraz** as vice-captain, also includes Soumya Sarkar, Shadman Islam, Mushfiqur Rahim, and uncapped pace bowler Musfik Hasan, added earlier as cover for the injured Nahid Rana. The tour continues with a three-day warm-up match against a Cricket Australia XI in Darwin from **August 6-8**, the first Test in Darwin from **August 13**, and the second and final Test in Mackay from **August 22**.
key_points: **Litton Das** has been added to Bangladesh's squad for the **first Test against Australia**, having earlier been expected to miss it.
He'd been sidelined by a **calf injury** picked up during the June ODI series against Australia.
The **first Test starts in Darwin on August 13**, preceded by a **three-day warm-up match (Aug 6-8)**.
The squad is captained by **Najmul Hossain Shanto**, with **Mehidy Hasan Miraz** as vice-captain.
The **second Test follows in Mackay from August 22**.

depth.background: Bangladesh is on its first Test tour of Australia in 23 years, already weakened by the absence of strike pacer Nahid Rana, out for the entire two-match series with a side strain. Litton Das, an experienced wicketkeeper-batter, had been expected to miss the tour's opening Test after a calf injury from the June ODI series against Australia, with his availability for the second Test uncertain. His return strengthens a batting order that will otherwise be tested against Australia's traditionally fast, bouncy home conditions.

thread.previously: When Bangladesh's squad departed for Australia on August 1, wicketkeeper-batter Litton Das was expected to miss the tour's opening Test after a calf issue, with strike pacer Nahid Rana ruled out of the entire series and uncapped quick Musfik Hasan added as cover.
thread.changed: Litton Das has now recovered faster than expected and been formally named in Bangladesh's squad for the first Test itself, restoring an experienced batting-and-wicketkeeping option ahead of the Darwin opener.

stories.title: Europe starts enforcing its first-ever law forcing AI chatbots to tell you you're talking to a machine
stories.what_happened: As of **August 2, 2026**, any AI system that talks directly to people — chatbots, voice assistants, customer-service bots — must tell users they're interacting with AI, unless that's already obvious from context. The European Commission formally began enforcing this and other AI Act transparency requirements this week. A related rule requiring **machine-readable watermarks on AI-generated content** (like deepfake videos or AI images) also starts now, though tools already on the market before August 2 get a grace period until December 2026 to comply. Companies that ignore the rules face fines of up to €15 million or 3% of their worldwide annual revenue.
key_points: **Article 50 of the EU AI Act** took effect August 2, and enforcement began this week
AI chatbots and voice assistants must now **disclose they're AI**, unless it's already obvious
AI-generated or edited content — including **deepfakes** — must eventually carry machine-readable marks
Content-marking rules have a **grace period until December 2026** for tools already on the market
Violators risk fines up to **€15 million or 3% of global annual turnover**, whichever is higher

depth.background: The **EU AI Act** is the world's first comprehensive law regulating artificial intelligence, passed by the European Union to manage AI risks by how dangerous a given use case is. One part of that law, Article 50, focuses specifically on **transparency** — making sure people know when they're dealing with a machine rather than a human, and when content (photos, video, audio) has been artificially generated or manipulated. Big tech platforms and AI developers have spent the past two years adjusting products to comply ahead of this deadline.

stories.title: F1 locks in Malaysia's comeback race after war forced Bahrain off the calendar
stories.what_happened: On **July 26, 2026**, F1 and the FIA confirmed that **Sepang International Circuit in Malaysia** would host the rescheduled event, officially billed as the '**Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia**,' on **October 2–4**. This week, the FIA finalised the last outstanding detail: the race will start at **3:00pm local time on Sunday, October 4** — the same slot Sepang used for its last F1 race in **2017**. The confirmation cleared up a brief scare among fans after F1's website mistakenly displayed Bahrain's old (much later, effectively night-race) start time due to what F1 called a systems error. Under the arrangement, **Bahrain's government is paying to stage the event** and keeps the Gulf Air title sponsorship and ticket revenue, even though the cars will be racing on the other side of Asia. The rescheduled race now slots into a demanding **triple-header** — three races in three consecutive weekends — alongside Azerbaijan (Baku) and Singapore.
key_points: The FIA has confirmed the relocated 2026 'Bahrain Grand Prix' will start at **3:00pm local time on October 4** at Sepang, Malaysia.
It's Malaysia's **first F1 race since 2017** — a nine-year gap — after Sepang was originally dropped from the calendar for low turnout.
The race was relocated after the **original Bahrain and Saudi Arabia Grands Prix were scrapped in March 2026** because of the region's conflict.
**Bahrain's government is funding the event** and keeps its Gulf Air title sponsorship and ticket revenue despite the venue switching countries.
The confirmed start time ends a week of confusion after F1's own website briefly listed the race at its old Bahrain (night-race) time by mistake.

depth.background: Formula 1's 2026 season was supposed to open with back-to-back races in the Gulf: **Bahrain (Sakhir)** and **Saudi Arabia**. In **March 2026**, both races were postponed and then scrapped after conflict in the region — stemming from the wider Iran-related Middle East crisis — made it unsafe to hold them. F1 spent months searching for a way to keep Bahrain's race on the calendar in some form rather than losing it outright for the year, since Bahrain had already committed sponsorship money and wanted to preserve its relationship with the sport.

stories.title: F1 boss Flavio Briatore wants a sprint race at all 24 Grands Prix — and Verstappen isn't happy
stories.what_happened: Speaking on The Race podcast, Alpine's Flavio Briatore proposed expanding Formula 1's Sprint race format from the current six Sprint weekends to all **24** rounds on the calendar, effectively creating a 48-event competitive season with both a Sprint and a Grand Prix at every venue. Briatore argued Friday practice sessions currently offer little value to spectators — 'you got two laps, you come back, and people are not here' — and that a genuine second competitive session each weekend would deliver far more for fans and broadcasters. The proposal directly clashes with drivers like Max Verstappen, who has repeatedly criticized the existing Sprint format as compressing practice time too much and adding unnecessary risk and strain on teams. F1 has already locked in six Sprint races for 2026, including new venues in Canada, the Netherlands, and Singapore, but Briatore's 'all 24' idea goes far beyond that.
key_points: Alpine executive **Flavio Briatore** has proposed adding a Sprint race to **all 24** F1 Grand Prix weekends, up from the current **six**.
His argument: Friday practice sessions are 'only technical' and give fans nothing to watch, so a second competitive race each weekend would add value.
The idea would effectively create a **48-event** competitive calendar across the season.
**Max Verstappen** has repeatedly criticized the sprint format as bad for racing and team operations, setting up a clash with Briatore's plan.
F1 has already confirmed **six** sprint races for 2026, including new sprint venues in **Canada, the Netherlands, and Singapore**.

depth.background: A 'Sprint' in F1 is a shorter, standalone race (about 100km, roughly a third the length of a normal Grand Prix) held on Saturday that awards its own points and helps set part of Sunday's grid — introduced in 2021 to add more competitive action to race weekends beyond a single Sunday race. Currently only six of F1's 24 weekends include a Sprint; the rest still follow the traditional format of two practice sessions, qualifying, and one race. Briatore, a longtime, high-profile F1 figure now a senior Alpine executive, has a history of pushing bold format changes, arguing F1 needs to keep evolving to hold fans' attention.

stories.title: Max Verstappen's father shuts down reports of a new exit-clause-free Red Bull contract
stories.what_happened: German outlet BILD reported that Red Bull has offered Max Verstappen a new contract extending his stay through **2029**, featuring a significant pay increase on top of his reported **€65 million** annual salary, on condition that he give up the **exit clauses** in his current deal. Those clauses reportedly let Verstappen leave early if he isn't inside the **top two of the drivers' championship** by the summer break — a threshold BILD says has now technically been triggered, with Verstappen currently down in **sixth place**. The report claimed Verstappen has until **October** to decide whether to activate his exit option, but that he is in no rush to sign the new offer either. His father, **Jos Verstappen**, responded directly on X, dismissing the report with the line 'You know absolutely nothing' — a blunt denial he has issued for previous driver-market rumors this season too.
key_points: German outlet **BILD** reported Red Bull has offered Max Verstappen a contract extension through **2029** with a big pay rise, in exchange for removing his **exit clause**

Verstappen's current deal reportedly lets him leave if he's **not inside the top two** in the championship by the summer break — a condition BILD says has now been **triggered**, since he sits **sixth**
His father, **Jos Verstappen**, publicly dismissed the report on X, writing simply: '**You know absolutely nothing**'
Max has previously confirmed he'll stay at Red Bull **for 2026**, but has repeatedly declined to commit beyond that

depth.background: Max Verstappen is a four-time F1 world champion whose current Red Bull contract runs through the end of 2028, but reportedly contains exit clauses tied to competitive performance. Red Bull's dominant recent run has faded in 2026 amid what insiders describe as wider team problems beyond just the car, fueling a season-long guessing game about Verstappen's future and pulling in rival teams like Mercedes and Aston Martin as rumored suitors. Jos Verstappen, himself a former F1 driver, frequently speaks publicly on his son's behalf and has a history of bluntly rejecting driver-market rumors he considers baseless.

stories.title: Ex-team boss Otmar Szafnauer says Aston Martin's F1 crisis is a 'five-year problem' of impatience, not bad luck
stories.what_happened: Otmar Szafnauer, Aston Martin's former team principal, said the root of the team's ongoing Formula 1 struggles goes back roughly **five years** to a pattern of wanting success too quickly under owner Lawrence Stroll, who has now owned the team for **eight years**. Szafnauer argued that chasing fast results caused excessive personnel turnover, and that the sport's most successful teams — he named Mercedes under Toto Wolff, Red Bull during its title-winning run, and Ferrari under former boss Ross Brawn — were all built on stability of personnel rather than constant change. He made the comments despite Aston Martin's heavy investment in recent years, including a new campus and wind tunnel, its new Honda engine partnership, and the high-profile signing of star designer Adrian Newey — none of which has yet translated into consistent on-track results in 2026.
key_points: Former Aston Martin principal **Otmar Szafnauer** says the team's struggles trace back **five years** to owner **Lawrence Stroll** wanting success **'too quickly.'**
He says chasing quick results caused **too much personnel turnover** — instability that has undercut the team ever since.
Szafnauer contrasts this with **Mercedes, Red Bull (in its winning years), and Ferrari under Ross Brawn** — all built on **stable personnel**.
Despite a **new campus, wind tunnel, Honda engine partnership**, and hiring star designer **Adrian Newey**, Aston Martin is still struggling in **2026**.
Stroll has owned the team for **eight years**.

depth.background: Aston Martin, under billionaire owner Lawrence Stroll, has spent heavily since 2018 to try to turn a mid-grid team into a championship contender — building new facilities, signing star personnel like design legend Adrian Newey, and partnering with Honda for engines starting in 2026. Despite the investment, the team has repeatedly underdelivered relative to its spending, and 2026 — the first season of new technical regulations and the Honda partnership — has been another difficult one, including Newey's own admission that his first year running the team was hampered by health issues. Otmar Szafnauer led the team as principal before departing, giving him an insider's view of what he says is its core problem.

stories.title: Honda says its once-strained Aston Martin partnership is 'getting better and better' ahead of a new engine debut
stories.what_happened: Honda Racing Corporation president **Koji Watanabe** said the relationship with Aston Martin, which was strained early in the 2026 season, has improved sharply as both sides prepare to combine the team's revised chassis with an upgraded power unit. Watanabe said the two sides are now in **'complete agreement'** on performance goals and testing plans. The technical progress has been visible on track: Aston Martin gained more than a second per lap with a heavily revised 'B'-specification car introduced at the Hungarian Grand Prix, where Fernando Alonso reached Q2 for the first time this season and both cars recovered positions in the race. Aston Martin ambassador Pedro de la Rosa echoed the sentiment, saying communication with Honda has 'incredibly improved at all levels.' Honda's new-specification engine completed its first on-track running during a filming day at the Hungaroring and is set to make its competitive race debut at the **Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort** after F1's summer break.
key_points: Honda Racing Corporation's president says the Aston Martin relationship is **'getting better and better'**
The partnership had a **disastrous start to 2026** — engine vibrations, reliability failures, and reported tension
Aston Martin gained **more than a second per lap** with its revised 'B'-spec car in Hungary
Fernando Alonso reached **Q2 for the first time all season** with the upgraded car
Honda's **new-spec power unit** is set to make its race debut at the Dutch Grand Prix after F1's summer break

depth.background: Aston Martin, led by legendary designer Adrian Newey, switched to Honda as its engine supplier for the new 2026 F1 rules cycle — a fresh start both sides hoped would deliver a leap forward. Instead, the season opened with severe engine vibrations and reliability problems, and reports emerged of friction over how to fix them. F1 teams and engine suppliers are locked in tight technical partnerships, so a breakdown in trust between them can slow development at exactly the moment a new rules era rewards teams that iterate fastest.

stories.title: Oscar Piastri says he'll be racing for McLaren in 2027, pushing back on speculation he'd make way for Verstappen
stories.what_happened: Speaking as F1's summer break began, Oscar Piastri was asked directly whether he could confirm he'll be racing for McLaren in 2027, and simply answered **'Yes.'** The comment directly rebuts a wave of reports — including claims he was preparing to exercise a contractual **release clause** reportedly tied to being outside the top five in the standings — suggesting he might leave the team, potentially to make room for Max Verstappen, whose own Red Bull contract includes a performance-linked exit clause. People close to Piastri have separately told media the exit talk is **'purely speculative.'** McLaren boss Zak Brown has also downplayed the broader Verstappen rumors as speculation with 'no conversations' behind them.
key_points: Piastri gave a **flat 'Yes'** when asked to confirm he'll be driving for McLaren in **2027**.
It directly contradicts reports he was about to trigger a **release clause** to leave the team.
That clause is reportedly tied to Piastri being **outside the top five** in the drivers' standings by summer.
The rumors were fueled by speculation that a Piastri exit could **clear a seat for Max Verstappen**.
Sources close to Piastri call any talk of him leaving **'purely speculative'**.

depth.background: McLaren has been F1's dominant team through the first half of 2026, and both its drivers, **Oscar Piastri** and **Lando Norris**, are under contract for 2027. But paddock speculation intensified this summer that **Max Verstappen** could leave Red Bull for McLaren — a move that would only make sense if one of McLaren's current drivers left, and Piastri's contract reportedly includes a **release clause** tied to his championship position that made him the more plausible one to go.

thread.previously: Reports said talks over a Verstappen move to McLaren for 2027 had reached their 'closing stages' as his Red Bull exit clause loomed.
thread.changed: Piastri has now publicly confirmed he expects to stay at McLaren in 2027, undercutting the theory that his seat is the one Verstappen would take.

stories.title: Red Bull reportedly offers to rip up Verstappen's exit clause with a $65m-a-year deal — Jos Verstappen shuts it down
stories.what_happened: According to Dutch media reports, **Red Bull has offered Max Verstappen a new one-year contract extension through 2029**, raising his salary to roughly **€65 million per season** in exchange for removing the exit clauses that have hung over the team all year. The clause currently gives Verstappen the right to leave between the summer break and October, since he finished the Hungarian Grand Prix weekend in **P6** in the standings — outside the top two threshold that would have kept the clause dormant. In response to the reports being shared on social media, **Jos Verstappen**, Max's father and a former F1 driver himself, flatly rejected them, posting **'You know absolutely nothing.'** The denial does not confirm or deny that talks are happening — it specifically challenges the accuracy of the reported terms, leaving observers unsure what to believe.
key_points: Red Bull is reported to have offered Max Verstappen a **one-year extension to 2029** worth around **€65 million a season**, with **no exit clauses**.
Verstappen's current contract lets him leave the team any time between the **summer break and October** if he isn't in the **top two of the standings** after the Hungarian GP.
After Hungary, Verstappen sits **P6** in the championship — meaning the exit clause is currently active and usable.
His father **Jos Verstappen** bluntly dismissed the reports on social media, writing **'You know absolutely nothing.'**
The denial leaves the F1 paddock guessing again just as Verstappen's Aston Martin and McLaren options were gathering momentum.

depth.background: Verstappen's Red Bull contract runs through **2028**, but it contains a rare **performance-linked exit clause**: if he isn't top two in the drivers' standings after the Hungarian Grand Prix, he can walk away from Red Bull between the summer break and October. That clause has fueled months of speculation since Red Bull's car has trailed **Mercedes and Ferrari** for much of 2026, with reported interest from **McLaren** and a surprise **Aston Martin** reunion with designer Adrian Newey. Red Bull, eager to keep its four-time champion, has been trying to negotiate the clause away before it can be triggered.

thread.previously: Verstappen's contract talks with McLaren were reported to have reached 'closing stages' as his Red Bull exit clause loomed, with a reunion with Adrian Newey at Aston Martin also floated as a shock third option.
thread.changed: Red Bull has now reportedly countered with a lucrative new offer to remove the exit clause entirely, but Jos Verstappen has publicly and bluntly denied the reported terms, leaving Verstappen's next move unclear.

stories.title: Bharti Airtel reports Q1 results today, with analysts penciling in a ~45% profit jump
stories.what_happened: Bharti Airtel is set to announce its **April–June (Q1 FY27) results** on August 4, with its earnings call scheduled for the following day. Ahead of the announcement, analysts polled by financial outlets expect **net profit to jump 26–45% year-on-year**, with some estimates as high as **₹8,638.60 crore**, alongside roughly **15% revenue growth**. Brokerages are watching subscriber additions (expected around 50–60 lakh net adds for the quarter), a modest uptick in ARPU to about **₹261**, and progress in turning Airtel's heavy 5G investment into sustained profit. The results land on one of the busiest days of India's Q1 earnings season, with **114 companies** — including ONGC, Pidilite, Marico, DLF, Sun Pharma Advanced Research, Aditya Birla Capital, Bosch and Shree Cement — also due to report.
key_points: Airtel's board meets today, **August 4**, to sign off on results for the quarter ended June 30.
Analysts expect net profit to rise **26–45% year-on-year**, with some estimates near **₹8,639 crore**.
Revenue is expected to grow around **15%**, helped by steady subscriber additions and 5G rollout.
**ARPU** (average revenue per user) is forecast to tick up to roughly **₹261/month**, a key profitability gauge.
It's one of **114 companies** reporting results today as India's Q1 earnings season hits its peak, alongside ONGC, Marico and DLF.

depth.background: Bharti Airtel is India's **second-largest telecom operator** by subscribers, competing chiefly with Reliance Jio and Vodafone Idea in a market that consolidated from more than a dozen players a decade ago to effectively three. Airtel has spent heavily to roll out **5G networks** across India and has steadily raised prepaid and postpaid tariffs in recent years to improve profitability after a brutal price war in the 2010s nearly wiped out smaller rivals. ARPU — how much revenue the company earns per subscriber each month — is the industry's single most-watched number because it shows whether tariff hikes are sticking without driving customers away.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon open a seventh round of US-brokered talks in Rome as Hezbollah calls them 'shameful'
stories.what_happened: Technical teams from Israel and Lebanon returned to Rome on **August 4** for a new round of US-brokered negotiations running through **August 6**. The talks are meant to advance the **framework peace agreement** the two countries signed last month, focusing on expanding the 'pilot zone' withdrawal-and-disarmament process and resolving outstanding **border disputes**. Lebanon's delegation, headed by diplomat Simon Karam and including military officers, ambassadors, lawyers and economic advisers, is pushing for a complete halt to Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon while talks are underway. Hezbollah publicly dismissed the negotiations as bringing "nothing but shame" on Lebanon and reiterated it will not disarm. Lebanon's prime minister hit back directly at Hezbollah, saying the group is the one that dragged the country into war in the first place. The US is pressing the Lebanese army to expand into pilot zones and the Israeli military to complete its withdrawal from them.
key_points: Technical teams meet in **Rome from August 4-6** for the **seventh round** of US-brokered talks.
Talks aim to implement a **framework peace agreement** signed last month, including phased **Israeli troop withdrawal** and Hezbollah **disarmament** in 'pilot zones'.
**Hezbollah** publicly rejected the process, calling it a source of 'nothing but shame' for Lebanon.
Lebanon's prime minister fired back, blaming Hezbollah for **dragging the country into war**.
Lebanon's delegation, led by diplomat **Simon Karam**, will demand a **full halt** to Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon during talks.

depth.background: Israel and Hezbollah fought a devastating war that ended with a ceasefire, and last month Lebanon and Israel signed a **framework agreement** meant to turn that truce into a lasting peace. The deal calls for Israel to withdraw from designated 'pilot zones' in stages while Lebanese forces disarm Hezbollah units inside them — a direct challenge to the Iran-backed group's decades-long status as an armed force operating outside the Lebanese state. Hezbollah, badly weakened in the war but still armed, has refused to accept being disarmed and calls the process illegitimate. This is now the **seventh round** of talks trying to translate that fragile framework into facts on the ground.

stories.title: Reports: Alonso could leave Aston Martin for Alpine in 2027, triggering a three-way driver swap with Sainz and Colapinto
stories.what_happened: Several Formula 1 outlets are reporting a potential three-way driver swap ahead of the 2027 season: Fernando Alonso moving from Aston Martin to Alpine, Carlos Sainz moving from Williams to Aston Martin to replace him, and Franco Colapinto returning to Williams to fill the seat Sainz would vacate. Reports say Alonso's talks with Alpine have 'accelerated' over the past month, helped by Alpine's incoming Gucci title sponsorship, which would give the team the budget to afford Alonso's salary. Aston Martin owner Lawrence Stroll has reportedly identified Sainz as his 'top candidate' to replace Alonso if he departs. Meanwhile, Alpine advisor Flavio Briatore has reportedly told Colapinto — currently driving for Alpine on loan — to start exploring other options, since Alpine may not extend his arrangement past this season; Colapinto's camp has reopened talks with Williams about a return. Alonso himself publicly maintains he has a contract with Aston Martin through 2027, though it's reported to include performance-linked conditions that could let him exit. None of the three drivers or teams have confirmed any part of this.
key_points: Multiple F1 outlets report **Fernando Alonso** is in 'accelerated' talks to leave Aston Martin for **Alpine** in 2027 — but none of this is confirmed by any team or driver.
Alpine's incoming **Gucci title sponsorship** is reportedly a key piece — it would help fund Alonso's high salary.
If Alonso leaves, Aston Martin owner **Lawrence Stroll** has reportedly identified **Carlos Sainz** (currently at Williams) as his top target to replace him.
That would open a seat at Williams for **Franco Colapinto**, who is currently on loan at Alpine — where advisor **Flavio Briatore** has reportedly told him to explore other options.
**Alonso publicly insists** he has a 2027 Aston Martin contract, though it reportedly includes performance-linked exit terms.

depth.background: F1's driver market moves on a roughly two-year cycle, and 2027 is a big one — new car regulations arrive that year, which often triggers drivers to reassess where they want to be. Fernando Alonso, a two-time world champion now in his mid-40s, has been at Aston Martin since 2023 but has long been linked with a possible return to Alpine, the team (formerly Renault) where he won both of his titles. Carlos Sainz joined Williams for the 2026 season after leaving Ferrari, and Franco Colapinto currently drives for Alpine on a loan-style arrangement rather than a full contract, making him the most exposed of the three if the music stops.

stories.title: Ferrari doubles down on frequent small upgrades over McLaren's big-package strategy, despite Wolff's cost-cap warning
stories.what_happened: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur confirmed the team will continue its strategy of bringing frequent, smaller upgrades to nearly every race weekend for the rest of the 2026 season, rather than adopting rival McLaren's approach of saving up for fewer, larger upgrade packages. 'We have a different philosophy,' Vasseur said. 'We try to bring new parts to every race.' Ferrari is reportedly planning a two-stage development push once the season resumes from its summer break: an aerodynamic update at the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort (August 21-23), followed by a power-unit upgrade — centered on a new turbocharger — timed for the Italian Grand Prix at Monza, Ferrari's home race. The announcement follows Mercedes boss Toto Wolff's comments questioning whether Ferrari can sustain this pace of updates without running out of cost-cap budget later in the season.
key_points: Ferrari team principal **Fred Vasseur** confirmed the team will keep bringing **small upgrades to nearly every race** rather than switching to McLaren's approach of fewer, bigger upgrade packages.
Ferrari is planning a **two-stage upgrade push** after the summer break: an **aerodynamic update at the Dutch GP (Zandvoort, Aug 21-23)**, followed by a new **turbocharger/engine upgrade for Monza**.
The plan comes right after Mercedes boss **Toto Wolff** publicly questioned how Ferrari can keep updating this often within F1's **cost cap**.
Ferrari driver **Charles Leclerc** has pushed the team to stay aggressive rather than let Mercedes and McLaren consolidate their advantage.
Vasseur's explanation: **'We have a different philosophy. We try to bring new parts to every race.'**

depth.background: Formula 1 has operated under a strict **cost cap** since 2021 — a hard annual spending limit designed to stop the richest teams from simply outspending everyone else on development. How a team spends that fixed budget — a few big, expensive upgrade packages versus many smaller, cheaper ones — has become a genuine strategic divide on the 2026 grid. Ferrari trails Mercedes and McLaren in the current championship battle and has repeatedly signaled it wants to keep pushing performance updates rather than conserve budget.

thread.previously: Yesterday, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff publicly questioned whether Ferrari could keep affording its frequent upgrade pace within F1's cost cap, suggesting the team would eventually run out of budget.
thread.changed: Ferrari has now confirmed it's sticking with that exact strategy — team principal Fred Vasseur says frequent small upgrades are a deliberate 'philosophy,' and detailed a specific two-stage upgrade plan for Zandvoort and Monza.
